page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.re8.240xlarge is an ultra-high-capacity instance in the memory-optimized server family, operating on the KVM hypervisor. The system is built on x86_64 architecture powered by Intel Xeon 8490H processors running at a base clock speed of 1.9 GHz. It allocates 960 dedicated vCPUs paired with 16,384 GB of system memory, providing approximately 17.07 GB of RAM per vCPU. Accelerators such as dedicated GPUs are not included with this instance type.

Network connectivity features a baseline throughput of 200 Gbps, providing significant interface bandwidth for large-scale data transfers. Local disk storage is not bundled, meaning all persistent data must be managed via remote or attached cloud storage volumes. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not provided by default.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides extreme resource consolidation, eliminating multi-node communication overhead for massive footprints that require coherent shared memory. However, the lack of local NVMe storage means performance for I/O-heavy workloads depends entirely on external block storage configurations. Alibaba Cloud ecs.re8.240xlarge is targeted at in-memory enterprise databases, extensive SAP HANA deployments, massive caching tiers, and large-scale analytical processing engines that require huge memory footprints on a single system.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.re8.240xlarge is an enterprise-scale memory-optimized instance built on KVM virtualization and the x86_64 architecture. Powered by 1.9 GHz Intel Xeon 8490H processors, the instance delivers 960 dedicated vCPUs alongside 16,384 GB of system memory, yielding 17.07 GB of RAM per vCPU core. It features a 200 Gbps baseline network throughput for data-intensive communication. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or hardware GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached block storage for persistent data requirements. With its massive compute core count and multi-terabyte memory footprint, ecs.re8.240xlarge eliminates node-clustering overhead for giant monolithic workloads. It is primarily engineered for very large in-memory databases, large-scale caching engines, real-time data streaming architectures, enterprise ERP systems, and memory-constrained analytical workloads requiring single-system memory cohesion.
